sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in connection with S.T. Case No.13 of 2021, pending on the file of learned Addl. Sessions Judge, Karanjia, arising out of Mahuldiha P.S. Case No.38 of 2020, for commission of alleged offences under Section 302/376/294/449 of the IPC.
3. Learned counsel, on instruction, submits that except the present BLAPL, no other bail application of the Petitioner relating to the aforementioned P.S. Case is pending in any other Court.

4. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Addl.
Sessions Judge, Karanjia by order dated 02.05.2024 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 16.08.2020 and as six witnesses have been examined in the meanwhile and they do not state about the complicity of the Petitioner, his further continuance in custody is not warranted.
6.
It is further submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner has been released on interim bail twice and has surrendered on time.
Such conduct ought to weigh with this Court in considering the bail application of the Petitioner.

7. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail referring to the disclosure statement of the Petitioner under Section 27 of the Evidence Act, which led to the discovery of the alleged weapon of offence- an axe.

The witnesses to the said 27 of the Evidence Act are Bhagirathi Mohanta, CSW-87 and Laban Birua, CSW-88.
8.

It is submitted with vehemence by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the statement of the parents of the deceased have been recorded number of times only to somehow implicate the petitioner as the Petitioner going to the house of the deceased.
Nothing is disclosed about complicity of the Petitioner, his further continuance in custody is not warranted.
9. It is further submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the prosecution has cited 103 witnesses, hence the trial is lingering.
Save and except the statement made by the Petitioner in custody, there is no other material to connect the Petitioner.
10. Such submission is opposed by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, referring to the tenor of the statements of the parents of the deceased.
11. Considering the nature of allegation, and CDR analysis thereof, this Court is not inclined to entertain the bail application at this stage.

12. Liberty is granted to the Petitioner to renew his prayer before the learned Court in seisin after examination of material witnesses including CSW-87 and 88.
13.
Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Soumya Signed by: SOUMYA RANJAN SAMAL
